newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cultus to name NZ oilfield partner soon.
newsitem.headline: Cultus to name NZ oilfield partner soon.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL expects to name a major international company as its partner for its Maari oil exploration project, offshore from Taranaki in New Zealand, in a week or two, managing director Don Beard said on Thursday.
"I would have thought in the next couple of weeks. It's a week or two away," Beard said.
Last month Beard told Reuters the Maari field could produce 100 million barrels of oil, making it one of New Zealand's largest oilfields.
Cultus had been reviewing a number of options for the offshore exploration licence area in the first quarter, but Beard said the company now knew which company would be involved in the project.
"We were looking at a number of people farming in. Now we know who we're going to do it with," he said.
Cultus plans to farm out about 70 percent of the investment to the as-yet-unnamed company, which Beard said would lead the project and cover the drilling costs of the first one or two wells.

Cultus intends to spud several wildcat -- high risk/high return -- oil wells this year which, along with its 25 percent stake in the promising Cornea oil discovery off Western Australia, could propel it into the big league.
Analysts believe Cornea could hold more than 500 million barrels of oil.

Beard said Cultus could soon be given the green light from the federal government for exploration at permits neighbouring the Cornea field, which it shares with partners Royal Dutch/Shell (50 percent) and Chevron Corp (25 percent).
He said securing the additional exploration blocks could double prospective production at Cornea.
"We tried to see if we could get a response yesterday, but still no news," Beard said, adding he was confident Cultus and its partners would secure the licences.
Cultus, listed in New Zealand and Australia, has seen its share price soar more than 600 percent over the past year on oil and gas discoveries and the prospects for more.
The stock leapt 33 cents higher last month on news of the Maari field's potential and the company's hopes for other projects.
At the time, Beard told Reuters Cultus was on track to become a A$1 billion (NZ$1.13 billion) company "in the next couple of years".
